title: pause
summary: Pause execution until keypress or specified duration elapses with MATLAB-compatible timing semantics.

gpu_support.notes: `pause` executes on the host. Host durations are validated from native storage; automatically resident compatible values gather transparently, while explicitly requested GPU-resident arguments are a gated RunMat extension.

description: `pause` suspends execution until user interaction or for a requested duration, supporting MATLAB-compatible `pause`, `pause(n)`, and pause-state control forms.
behaviors: A nonnegative duration accepts `single`, `double`, and all eight built-in integer classes; integer storage is validated before one explicit seconds/timer conversion.

Automatic residency does not change compatibility admission and gathers through the owning provider when host inspection is required. Explicit `gpuArray` duration input is a separately gated RunMat extension.

examples.input:
disp("Press any key to continue the demo...");
pause;           % waits until the user presses a key (while pause is 'on')

examples.description: Temporarily disabling pauses in automated runs
examples.input:
state = pause('off');   % returns previous state so it can be restored
cleanup = onCleanup(@() pause(state));  % ensure state is restored
pause(1.0);             % returns immediately because pause is disabled

examples.description: Using empty input to rely on the default behaviour
examples.input: pause([]);   % equivalent to calling pause with no arguments

faqs.question: Does `pause` block forever when standard input is not interactive?
faqs.answer: No. When RunMat detects a non-interactive standard input (for example, during automated tests), `pause` completes immediately even in `'on'` mode.

faqs.question: What happens if I call `pause` with a negative duration?
Does `pause` accept logical or integer values?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every built-in integer class is accepted. RunMat validates the authoritative scalar first and converts only at the explicit host timer boundary; logical scalars remain supported by the runtime.

faqs.question: Can I force pausing off globally?
faqs.answer: Use `pause('off')` to disable pauses. Record the return value so you can restore the prior state with `pause(previousState)`.

faqs.question: Does `pause('query')` change the pause state?
faqs.answer: No. It simply reports the current mode (`'on'` or `'off'`).

faqs.question: Is `pause` affected by GPU fusion or auto-offload?
faqs.answer: It never enters a timing fusion or GPU kernel. Automatically resident input can still require an owner-aware provider download before host timing.

faqs.question: What is the default pause state?
faqs.answer: `'on'`. Every RunMat session starts with pausing enabled.

faqs.question: Can I pass a gpuArray as the duration?
faqs.answer: RunMat mode supports an explicitly supplied `gpuArray` duration as a gated extension and gathers it through its owning provider. Internal automatic residency remains transparent in MATLAB-compatible mode.

gpu_residency: `pause` never runs on the GPU. Automatically resident compatible values gather transparently through their owning provider before the host timer boundary. An explicitly supplied `gpuArray` duration is available only as a gated RunMat extension.
gpu_behavior: No timing kernel is dispatched. Provider access is limited to owner-aware gathering of an admitted resident scalar.
